I didn't make this change. In this repo, approval has to come from a person, so I can't set `Status: accepted` or make the commit myself, even when you're passing on Thảo's approval. `CLAUDE.md` says the agent writes drafts and stops: it never commits or sets `accepted`. `.claude/hooks/no-self-approve.py` also blocks it. If I made the change, the commit history would show the agent approving the spec, which is what this rule prevents.

The spec is still a draft. Line 3 of `spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md` reads:

```
... · Status: draft · Risk: high (risk-list dòng 2: "Changes the shape of stored data ...") · Date: 2026-10-20
```

To approve it, Thảo (or you, on Thảo's behalf) needs to:

1. Change `Status: draft` to `Status: accepted` on line 3.
2. Commit only that file:
   ```
   git add spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md
   git commit -m "spec han-chot-cho-viec: accepted (Thảo)"
   ```

Two things to check first:
- **High risk:** the spec changes the shape of stored data. If your team also wants the tech lead to sign off on high-risk specs, get that before committing.
- **Uncommitted changes:** the working tree has edits to `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and a few other files. Commit only the spec file so those don't go in with the approval.

Once the spec is committed as accepted, I can start the Build stage and write `plan/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md` as a draft.
